column12: JUDGEMENT on the comparator and the reference weight. The caller asked for Exondys via lookup.py demand, but the book holds no drug_demand row for Exondys 51, Vyondys 53, Amondys 45 or Elevidys (checked by brand name and by asset_id 107), data.cms.gov is blocked from this container (403), and two searches did not surface its CMS Part B figure. A published WAC beats the CMS convention in any case. Exondys is the only marketed exon 51 skipper and z-rostudirsen seeks the same label, so it is priced at parity. Case for higher: price is weight-based and EVOLVE's commercial eteplirsen patients averaged 14.0 years of age, heavier than 30 kg (at 45 kg the same WAC gives $1,123,200); the $16/mg WAC dates from 2019 and later increases were not checked; Dyne may ask a premium for monthly rather than weekly infusions and higher dystrophin. Case for lower: DELIVER enrolled ages 4 to 16 and a 20 kg boy costs $499,200; Sarepta's own launch statement put the average near $300,000 a year (BioPharma Dive, as above); payers may resist a second accelerated approval in the same exon.

column12: How the pool is restricted: the book's all-DMD prevalence and incidence are multiplied by the 13% whose mutation is amenable to exon 51 skipping, 11,952 x 0.13 = 1,554 US patients plus 48 a year. That is the only filter. No age or ambulatory filter is applied, because the BLA asks for the whole exon 51-amenable population (Exondys's label has neither restriction) and DELIVER enrolled both ambulant and non-ambulant boys aged 4 to 16 (8-K 0001193125-26-009782). JUDGEMENT that the label follows the BLA. Case for lower: FDA could restrict an accelerated approval to DELIVER's ages or to ambulatory patients (FORZETTO is ambulatory only, ages 4 to 18), and only genetically confirmed patients are addressable. The 13% comes from a 2009 database; the TREAT-NMD database (Bladen CL et al., Hum Mutat 2015, PMID 25604253) reports exon-skipping applicability overall, not by exon, in its abstract

The ratio was 0.184 in 2024 and 2023 and 0.129 in 2022 (FY2024 10-K 0000950170-25-029973). Sarepta's ex-US sales come through distributors in South America, Europe and the Middle East without an EU approval: the book's EMA register lists Exondys (eteplirsen, EMEA/H/C/004355) as Refused, and golodirsen and casimersen are absent.
